{{ElectionsCO}}

The '''2026 Colorado gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Colorado]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Jared Polis]] is [[Term limits in the United States|ineligible]] to seek re-election to a third consecutive term. [[Primary elections]] took place on June 30, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025 |title=2026 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|website= NCSL |access-date=5 August 2025}}</ref>

In the Democratic primary, Colorado Attorney General [[Phil Weiser]] defeated U.S. senator [[Michael Bennet]]. If elected, Weiser would be the second consecutive Jewish governor after Polis. The [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] has not won a gubernatorial election in Colorado since [[2002 Colorado gubernatorial election|2002]] nor a statewide office since 2016.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Times |first=The New York |date=2017-08-01 |title=Colorado University Regents-At-Large Results: Heidi Ganahl Leads |url=https://www.nytimes.com/elections/2016/results/colorado-university-regents-at-large |access-date=2026-04-24 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Republican nominee [[Victor Marx]]'s candidacy has been mired in controversy; Marx has made a number of dubious claims and has notably stated he is unsure how many people he has killed.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Full interview: Colorado Republican gubernatorial candidate Victor Marx |url=https://www.9news.com/video/news/politics/full-interview-colorado-republican-gubernatorial-candidate-victor-marx/73-c7e83d54-e098-41c0-b4fb-15457b261b06 |website=9News |language=en-US |access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref> Leading to the Republican primary, both of Marx's opponents indicated they would refuse to endorse him if he won the nomination.<ref name="Luning 2026">{{Cite web |last=Luning |first=Ernest |date=May 27, 2026 |title=Republicans Kirkmeyer, Bottoms say they won’t back Marx if he wins Colorado’s gubernatorial primary |url=https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/05/27/republicans-kirkmeyer-bottoms-say-they-wont-back-marx-if-he-wins-colorados-gubernatorial-primary/ |website=Colorado Politics |language=en-US |access-date=July 21, 2026}}</ref>

== Democratic primary ==
=== Candidates ===
To move forward to the primary, candidates had to petition onto the ballot or achieve 30% or more at the [[Colorado Democratic Party]] State Assembly. Michael Bennet was the only candidate to petition onto the primary ballot. All other candidates went through the State Assembly process. [[Phil Weiser]] was the only candidate to achieve 30% or more.<ref>{{cite news |work=[[Colorado Democratic Party]] |access-date=March 28, 2026 |url=https://www.coloradodems.org/press/colorado-democratic-party-concludes-2026-state-assembly-announces-results?fbclid=IwY2xjawQ1WJ9leHRuA2FlbQIxMQBicmlkETFGQmVobEtQV1Vubk5hT1M0c3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABHq17U9MKJ8KzaqEtc_RpLGbfqCD74CWiN0D8uLv96FJS6y-4SGjmCPvQ-I4j_aem_tWJWw7WdgcoqyIBfcyphrw |title=Colorado Democratic Party Concludes 2026 State Assembly, Announces Results}}</ref> Bennet's petition was deemed sufficient on March 24, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |work=Colorado Secretary of State |access-date=April 15, 2026 |url=https://www.coloradosos.gov/pubs/elections/vote/primaryPetitionCandidates.html |title=2026 Primary Election Petition Candidates Who Submitted Petition Signatures}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==
=== Candidates ===
To move forward to the primary, candidates had to petition onto the ballot or achieve 30% or more at the [[Colorado Republican Party]] State Assembly. [[Barbara Kirkmeyer]] was the only candidate to petition onto the primary ballot. Her petition was deemed sufficient on April 15, 2026.<ref>{{cite news |work=Colorado Secretary of State |access-date=April 15, 2026 |url=https://www.coloradosos.gov/pubs/elections/vote/primaryPetitionCandidates.html |title=2026 Primary Election Petition Candidates Who Submitted Petition Signatures}}</ref> All other candidates went through the State Assembly process. [[Scott Bottoms]] and [[Victor Marx]] were the only candidates to achieve 30% or more.<ref name="Assembly">{{cite news |work=The Colorado Sun |access-date=April 12, 2026 |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/04/11/scott-bottoms-gop-primary-ballot-colorado-governor/ |title=State Rep. Scott Bottoms secures top spot on Republican primary ballot for Colorado governor}}</ref>

==== Nominee ====
*[[Victor Marx]], ministry leader<ref name="Marx">{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2025/10/03/ministry-founder-high-risk-missionary-victor-marx-joins-colorados-republican-gubernatorial-primary/|title=Ministry founder, 'high-risk' missionary Victor Marx joins Colorado's Republican gubernatorial primary|last=Luning|first=Ernest|date=October 3, 2025|access-date=October 3, 2025|website=[[The Colorado Statesman|Colorado Politics]]}}</ref>
**Running mate: George Markert, AI strategic advisor<ref>{{cite news |work=[[CBS News]] |access-date=August 20, 2026 |author=Swanson, Christa |date=August 1, 2026 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/colorado-republican-gubernatorial-nominee-chooses-running-mate/ |title=Colorado Republican gubernatorial nominee Victor Marx chooses running mate}}</ref>

==== Eliminated in primary ====
*[[Scott Bottoms]], [[Colorado House of Representatives|state representative]] from the 15th district (2023–present)<ref name=bottoms>{{cite news |last1=Paul |first1=Jesse |title=Scott Bottoms, Republican state representative, will run for Colorado governor in 2026 |url=https://coloradosun.com/2025/01/20/scott-bottoms-colorado-governor-2026/ |access-date=January 20, 2025 |work=[[The Colorado Sun]] |date=January 20, 2025}}</ref>
*[[Barbara Kirkmeyer]], [[Colorado Senate|state senator]] from the [[Colorado's 23rd Senate district|23rd district]] (2021–present), candidate for [[Colorado's 4th congressional district]] in [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado#District 4|2014]], and nominee for [[Colorado's 8th congressional district]] in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado#District 8|2022]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Paul |first1=Jesse |title=Republican Barbara Kirkmeyer is running to be Colorado's next governor |url=https://coloradosun.com/2025/09/09/barbara-kirkmeyer-colorado-governor-2026/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |work=The Colorado Sun |date=September 9, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Assembly" />

==== Eliminated at convention ====
*Jason Clark, money manager, candidate for governor in [[2014 Colorado gubernatorial election|2014]] and independent candidate in [[2010 Colorado gubernatorial election|2010]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Metzger |first1=Hannah |title=Third Time's the Charm? Jason Clark Is Running for Colorado Governor...Again |url=https://www.westword.com/news/third-times-the-charm-jason-clark-running-colorado-governor-23107563 |access-date=January 22, 2025 |work=[[Westword]] |date=January 22, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
*Joshua Griffin, research and development firm founder and candidate for {{ushr|CO|5}} in [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado#District 5|2024]]<ref name="Marx" />
*Will McBride, attorney<ref name="Marx" />
*Jason Mikesell, [[Teller County]] sheriff<ref>{{cite news |last1=Watson |first1=Lauren |title=Teller County Sheriff Jason Mikesell running for Colorado governor |url=https://www.kktv.com/2025/03/13/teller-county-sheriff-jason-mikesell-running-colorado-governor/ |access-date=March 13, 2025 |work=[[KKTV]] |date=March 13, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==== Withdrawn ====
*[[Mark Baisley]], [[Colorado Senate|state senator]] from the [[Colorado's 4th Senate district|4th district]] (2023–present) (''[[2026 United States Senate election in Colorado|running for U.S. senate]]'')<ref name="Lopez"/>
*[[Greg Lopez]], former [[U.S. representative]] from {{ushr|CO|4}} (2024–2025) and candidate for governor in [[2018 Colorado gubernatorial election|2018]] and [[2022 Colorado gubernatorial election|2022]] ''(running as an Independent)''<ref name="Lopez">{{cite news |last1=Boyd |first1=Shaun |title=Former Colorado Republican congressman leaves the GOP, reshuffling the gubernatorial race |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/greg-lopez-colorado-governor-race-unaffiliated-candidate/ |access-date=January 6, 2026 |work=[[CBS News]] |date=January 5, 2026}}</ref>
